plantName: Used to save it and to group its history, checklist, photos and report. If you leave it blank, the app uses the coordinates as identifier.
coords: Plant location: used to calculate the sun position and to fetch weather data. In the field tap Get my GPS position; remotely, paste the Google Maps coordinates (41.45, 2.24) into the latitude field and they are split automatically.
kwp: Peak power of the PV array: no. of modules × Wp of each ÷ 1000. E.g.: 40 modules of 450 Wp = 18 kWp. It appears in the design, the installation certificate or the monitoring portal.
pac:
Maximum inverter output power (or the export limit if the plant has zero export). If the array can deliver more, the inverter clips (clipping) and the app will not count it as a fault.
DC/AC = kWp ÷ inverter kW; typically 1.1–1.3.
orient: Which way the panels face. In degrees: 0° = South, −90° = East, +90° = West, ±180° = North. E.g.: South-east = −45°, South-west = +45°. If unsure, check the Google Maps satellite view.
tilt:
Panel angle relative to the ground: 0° = horizontal, 90° = vertical. Flush-mounted on tiles is usually 10–20°; triangle mounts on flat roofs, 20–35°.
With Use phone level you measure it by laying the phone flat on the module glass.
year: Modules lose performance over the years (≈0.5 %/year; configurable in Settings). With the year entered, the app does not expect a 10-year-old plant to perform like a new one. If left blank, it is treated as new.
arrays:
For East-West roofs, pitched roofs or panels facing several directions. Split the power into arrays (each with its own kWp, orientation and tilt) and the app calculates the irradiance of each separately and adds them up.
East-West template: splits the kWp equally between East (−90°) and West (+90°).
plants: Save the plants you visit often to check them remotely. Each one keeps its module datasheet, string configuration, history, checklist and photos.
realKw: Power the inverter or portal shows right now, in kW (AC side). Read it just after tapping Analyse. If a cloud passes, wait for it to settle and repeat.
ring:
Actual power ÷ expected power with the irradiance, temperature and losses at this moment.
🟢 ≥ 85 %: OK · 🟡 70–85 %: check shading or soiling · 🔴 < 70 %: possible string, protection or inverter fault.
The PR (IEC 61724) shown below does not account for temperature or losses: in a healthy plant it is usually between 75 and 85 %.
dev: How far actual production is from expected, in %. Negative = producing less than it should.
loss: kW missing right now compared with expected. Gives you an idea of what the fault is costing.
mPoa: Solar radiation reaching the panel surface (with its orientation and tilt), according to Open-Meteo. Below, the clear-sky value: the theoretical maximum for this time.
mPexp: AC power the plant should deliver right now with the actual weather, after losses and temperature, and limited by the inverter. Below, what it would deliver under clear sky.
mClouds: Percentage of sky covered. Between 30 and 80 % the irradiance changes within seconds and the instant reading is unreliable: in that case rely more on the daily energy.
mTcell: Estimated cell temperature (NOCT model). The panel loses ~0.35 % of power per degree above 25 °C; in summer an 8–10 % loss from heat alone is normal. Below, the ambient temperature.
chart: Dashed line: clear-sky production. Green area: forecast with today's actual weather. Yellow dot: your inverter reading. Yellow line: inverter limit (if entered).
strings:
All strings receive the same sun, so comparing them detects faults without depending on irradiance. The reference is the median (violet line), so a faulty string does not distort it.
Measure them all within 2–3 minutes so the sun does not change.
strUnit: Current (A): with a DC clamp meter on each string, or from the portal. Power (kW): per MPPT from the portal; in that case enter the no. of modules to compare strings of different lengths.
strMod: Modules in series in that string. Power mode only: the app compares W per module so that a 10-module string does not look faulty next to a 12-module one.
strDev: Difference from the median. 🟢 ±5 % · 🟡 −5 to −15 % (shading, soiling, mismatch) · 🔴 < −15 % or no production (open string, fuse, MC4, diode).
modVoc: Open-circuit voltage of one module at STC. On the datasheet: Voc / Open-circuit voltage.
modIsc: Short-circuit current of one module at STC. On the datasheet: Isc / Short-circuit current.
modPmax: Module rated power in Wp (Pmax / Maximum power).
modVmp: Voltage at the maximum power point (Vmpp). Optional: used to estimate the string operating point.
modImp: Current at the maximum power point (Impp). Optional.
modSeries: How many modules in series the string you are about to measure has. The string Voc is the sum of all its modules.
modBeta: How much the voltage drops per degree of heat. Datasheet: Temperature coefficient of Voc, typically −0.25 to −0.30 %/°C.
modAlpha: How much the current rises with temperature. Datasheet: Temperature coefficient of Isc, typically +0.04 to +0.06 %/°C.
modCells: Cells in series in the module: 60, 66 or 72 (half-cut modules with 120/132/144 half cells count as 60/66/72). If left blank, it is estimated from Voc.
condG: By default, the one from the last analysis (satellite data). If you carry a reference cell or solar meter, enter its reading: the expected Isc will be much more accurate.
condT: By default, the estimated value. If possible, measure the module back with an IR thermometer and add ~2 °C. Every 10 °C of error changes the expected Voc by ~3 %.
measVoc: DC voltage between + and − of the string open-circuit (disconnector open, no load). ⚠️ Use a CAT III 1000 V DC multimeter or higher and insulating gloves.
measIsc: String short-circuit current with suitable equipment (PV tester or DC clamp with the string safely short-circuited). Never short-circuit a string with the multimeter probes.
vocExp: What you should read now: module Voc corrected for temperature and irradiance × no. of modules. Tolerance ±3 %. If ~1 module Voc is missing, a module is bypassed; if ~1/3 is missing, a bypass diode.
energy: Today (so far): energy since sunrise. Yesterday (full day): the whole day, the most reliable figure. The app adds up hour by hour what it should have produced with the actual irradiance.
eReal: kWh produced that day according to the inverter or portal (not the cumulative total since installation).
eExp: kWh the plant should have produced that day with the actual weather, limited by the inverter if you entered its AC power.
ePi: Actual energy ÷ expected energy. Same thresholds as the traffic light: ≥ 85 % OK. As it averages the whole day, passing clouds do not distort it.
eYield: Energy ÷ peak power = equivalent full-power hours. Lets you compare plants of different sizes. In Spain, a good summer day is around 5–7 kWh/kWp.
imp:
In the inverter portal look for Reports / Statistics / Export and download the daily (best) or hourly production as CSV or Excel. The app detects the date and energy column on its own; if it gets it wrong, correct it in the drop-downs.
It then downloads the actual weather for each day (Open-Meteo, up to 1 year back; needs a connection) and calculates day-by-day performance with the plant configuration from Diagnosis.
impType: Energy per period: kWh produced that day (or that hour). Average power: kW in each 5, 15 or 60 min interval (the app integrates them). Cumulative meter: total kWh since installation (the app subtracts each day from the previous one).
rain: Days since the last rainfall of at least 1 mm. In dry weather soiling builds up and production drops; rain partly cleans the panels.
nextRain: Forecast for the next 3 days. If rain is coming soon, it may be worth waiting before scheduling a cleaning.
check:
OK = correct · ✕ = defect (add a note and photo: it will appear in red in the report) · N/A = not applicable to this installation. Anything left unmarked appears as «not checked».
Saved per plant until you tap New inspection.
report:
Gathers everything you measured during the visit. Technician and company are remembered for future reports; client, remarks and next inspection are saved per plant.
Download PDF saves it on the phone; Share PDF sends it straight via WhatsApp, email or Drive (if the browser does not allow it, it is downloaded).
New inspection clears the checklist, photos and remarks for this plant (history is kept): generate the PDF first.
sign: The responsible technician signs with a finger (or stylus) and the signature appears at the end of the PDF next to their name, position and date. Name and position are remembered; the signature belongs to each inspection and is cleared with New inspection.
cal:
Creates an all-day event on the next inspection date (avoiding Saturdays and Sundays) with the plant, client, performance and outstanding defects from this visit, plus the location to open it in Maps.
Google Calendar needs a connection; the .ics file works without data and is valid for iPhone, Outlook or Samsung (includes a reminder 7 days before).
photos: Stored only on this phone, reduced in size and stamped with date, time, coordinates and plant, like site cameras. Photos taken from a checklist defect are marked as DEFECT in the PDF.
history: Each Save diagnosis adds a point (large size = daily data). The %/month trend is calculated by regression; a jump of more than 8 % is marked as «cleaning?» and the trend is recalculated from there.
quick: Short version to paste into WhatsApp, an email or the client portal, without attachments.
sModel: Parameters used to calculate the expected power throughout the app. They apply to all plants.
sLosses:
Everything lost between panel and meter: wiring, inverter, normal soiling, mismatch, degradation. Default 14 %. New plant: 10–12 %; old or with long cable runs: 15–18 %.
⚠️ The higher it is, the less demanding the traffic light: do not raise it to «hide» a problem.
sGamma: Power the module loses per degree above 25 °C (datasheet: Temperature coefficient of Pmax). PERC ≈ −0.35 · TOPCon ≈ −0.30 · Heterojunction ≈ −0.26 %/°C.
sNoct: Temperature the cell reaches at 800 W/m², 20 °C and light wind; used to estimate the actual temperature. Ventilated triangle mount: 43–45 °C · Flush-mounted on roof: 48–50 °C · Integrated without ventilation: 50–55 °C.
sDegr: Module power loss per year of operation. Typical warranties: 0.4–0.55 %/year (mono PERC/TOPCon); older or thin-film modules, 0.7–1 %/year. Only applied if you enter the commissioning year.
sAlbedo: Light reflected by the ground onto the panels (only counts if they are tilted). Soil, grass or concrete: 0.2 · Light gravel: 0.3 · White membrane: 0.5–0.7 · Snow: 0.8.
sScreen: High contrast: light background and dark text for reading in full sun (also with the ☀️ button above). Show help: turns these question marks on or off.
sFeedback: Opens a form to suggest improvements or report bugs. It is published on GitHub (you need a free account) along with the version and browser, never with your plant data.
sBackup:
Everything is stored only in this browser: if you clear it or change phone, it is lost. Create backup downloads a file with plants, modules, history, checklists and photos; save it to Drive or email it to yourself. Restore replaces the current data with the backup (asks for confirmation).
Clear cache forces fresh weather data to be fetched on the next analysis (normally reused for 5 min).
